\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ટાયર} (ṭāyar)}{ટાયર (ṭāyar)}]{\gu{ટાયર} (ṭāyar) — a tyre}

\label{lesson:GU-C401-tayar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a handlebar, then the Gujarati for to toss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ટાયર}}
\textbf{\gu{ટાયર}} — \emph{ṭāyar} — \textquotedblleft{}a tyre\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ગાડીના} \gu{ટાયરમાં} \gu{હવા} \gu{ઓછી} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{gāḍīnā ṭāyarmā̃ havā ochī che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is too little air in the car's tyre.
\end{quote}

A neuter noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ટાયર}} (\emph{ṭāyar}) is borrowed from English \emph{tyre}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭāyar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭāyar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gāḍīnā ṭāyarmā̃ havā ochī che.} — There is too little air in the car's tyre.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a handlebar, then the Gujarati for to toss, then say \emph{ṭāyar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ટાયર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tyre\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a tyre, then the Gujarati for a puncture.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઘસડવું} (ghasaḍvũ)}{ઘસડવું (ghasaḍvũ)}]{\gu{ઘસડવું} (ghasaḍvũ) — to drag}

\label{lesson:GU-C401-ghasadvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a puncture, then the Gujarati for a truck.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઘસડવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ઘસડવું}} — \emph{ghasaḍvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to drag\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તે} \gu{ભારે} \gu{પટારો} \gu{રસ્તા} \gu{પર} \gu{ઘસડે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{te bhāre paṭāro rastā par ghasḍe che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He drags the heavy trunk along the road.
\end{quote}

Past, with \gu{તેણે} (he or she …): \gu{તેણે} \gu{પટારો} \gu{ઘસડ્યો}, \emph{teṇe paṭāro ghasaḍyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ઘસડવું}} (\emph{ghasaḍvũ}) seems to be built on the root of the Gujarati verb \emph{ghasvũ}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under Sanskrit \emph{gharṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}rubs\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4450): what you drag rubs along the ground. CDIAL gives no form for \gu{ઘસડવું} itself, so the link is hedged.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghasaḍvũ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghasaḍvũ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{te bhāre paṭāro rastā par ghasḍe che.} — He drags the heavy trunk along the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for a puncture, then the Gujarati for a truck, then say \emph{ghasaḍvũ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{ઘસડવું} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To drag\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઉથલવું} (uthalvũ)}{ઉથલવું (uthalvũ)}]{\gu{ઉથલવું} (uthalvũ) — to overturn; to tip over}

\label{lesson:GU-C401-uthalvu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for a truck, then the Gujarati for to drag.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઉથલવું}}
\textbf{\gu{ઉથલવું}} — \emph{uthalvũ} — \textquotedblleft{}to overturn; to tip over\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{ખાડામાં} \gu{પડીને} \gu{ટ્રક} \gu{ઉથલી} \gu{ગઈ}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khāḍāmā̃ paḍīne ṭrak uthlī gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The truck fell into a pit and overturned.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \gu{તે} \gu{ટ્રક} \gu{ઉથલી} \gu{ગઈ}, \emph{te ṭrak uthlī gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ઉથલવું}} (\emph{uthalvũ}) goes back to \emph{*utthalati}, \textquotedblleft{}is upset, is turned over\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs; CDIAL lists the Gujarati verb (CDIAL 1805).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
